neighboring_unit_entries.title: Exponent-smoothed Möbius approximation
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Replacing mu(q)/q by mu(q)/q^(1+epsilon_n), with epsilon_n tending to zero no faster than the stated logarithmic threshold, preserves coordinatewise convergence to -E1 and the O(n/p) far-tail estimate. The proof rewrites divisor sums by Euler products and controls zeta-tail errors directly.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Triangular correction, raw Möbius weighting, and exponent smoothing all solve fixed-coordinate convergence and admit automatic remote-tail control; they differ in exact low-coordinate cancellation and in the moving interval on which a common square-summable majorant remains necessary.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: All three RH conclusions are conditional on an unproved domination hypothesis for infinitely many n; coordinatewise limits and big-O tails alone do not give Hilbert-norm convergence.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Three approximation schemes isolate moving domination windows

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The natural scheme's exact low-coordinate energy forces simultaneous cancellation in Möbius partial sums, revealing a concrete obstruction that the smoothed weights are designed to soften while preserving the same target coordinates.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source does not prove that smoothing removes the unconditional obstruction; its strongest positive efficiency statement assumes RH and cites prior work.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Low-coordinate energy motivates smoothing but does not validate it unconditionally
